Okay, so before you order, let me run you through tonight's specials. The first one is a roasted half chicken. It's rubbed with a garlic and rosemary seasoning, and it comes with two sides. Tonight we've got roasted carrots or the mashed potatoes. The second one is the steak. That's an eight-ounce cut, and the kitchen recommends it medium rare, so it's still pink in the middle. It goes with a mushroom sauce, but I can bring that on the side if you'd rather. And the third one is a white bean soup, which is our hearty option. It's mild, no spice at all, and honestly, it's the one I'd order. Oh, and the house salad tonight comes with a lemon dressing. It's pretty tangy, so if that's not your thing, just say the word and I'll swap it out. Any questions before I put that in?

Hi, this message is for Gisele Gallego. I'm calling from Maple and Vine on Connecticut Avenue to confirm your reservation for Friday the fourteenth, at seven thirty, party of four, under the name Gallego. Just a couple of things before you come in. We hold the table for fifteen minutes, so if you're running late, give us a call and we'll do our best. Also, you noted a nut allergy on the booking, so I passed that along to the kitchen. Two of our dressings are made with almonds, but the chef can do a substitution on any of them, no problem at all. And one more thing. Parking on that block is tough after six, so I'd use the garage on the corner. Give us a call back if anything changes. Otherwise, we'll see you Friday. Thanks.

I mean, the thing nobody warns you about is the seasoning. You can learn a hundred nouns, you know, the names of the vegetables, the cuts of meat, and you still open a menu here and have no idea what you're about to eat. Because it's never just chicken, right? It's chicken with a smoked paprika rub, or an herb crust, and if you don't know what an herb is doing in that sentence, the whole dish disappears on you. And the adjectives are the worst part. Savory, tangy, mild. Those three words tell you more about a plate than the name of the dish does. Back home I could taste something and name it. Here I taste it and I've got nothing. So what I do now is I just ask. I ask what's in it, every single time, and honestly, nobody minds. That's the part that took me two years to work out.
